closes: C7. No flow anywhere patches Portal Registry, so a citizen can only ever be shown what SUBMISSION wrote. Six of the seven governed status values are unreachable.
decision: D1 - a second branch on the existing crossing, not a new flow and not a SharePoint trigger. There is nothing to trigger on: ECM_DOCS_INTAKE is a live read feed, not a copy, and no flow in the estate creates an internal row from portal data.
triggerUnchanged: HTTP POST, triggerAuthenticationType = Tenant. An anonymous caller cannot invoke this flow before or after.

structure.wrap: Wrap the existing Scope_Global_Intake_Feed in a Switch. Move nothing inside it.

cases.feed: The existing Scope_Global_Intake_Feed, byte for byte. This is also the default, so every caller sending no action keeps the behaviour it has today.

createFirst.name: Scope_Writeback
createFirst.where: a new case on the Switch that wraps Scope_Global_Intake_Feed
createFirst.note: The three actions above are placed inside it, so the scope has to exist before they can be. The patcher's placement pass is a fixpoint and will retry them until it does.

actions.name: Get_Registry_Row_By_Reference
actions.why: Missing reference is a 404, not a create. This branch never inserts into the registry - only the portal may do that.

actions.name: Patch_Registry_Status
actions.why: Status must be one of the seven governed keys in config/status-vocabulary.config.js. Reject anything else rather than writing a word the portal cannot render.

actions.name: Create_Timeline_Event
actions.why: The timeline is what the citizen actually reads. A status patched without an event is a change nobody can see.

requestShape.note: With the assigned unit for technical assessment.

clientChange.add: PORTAL_STATUS_WRITEBACK: Object.freeze({ method:'POST', action:"writeback", write:true, sourceKey:"SCAN_INTAKE", url:EndpointUrls.SCAN_INTAKE }),
clientChange.why: Same flow, same URL, different fixed action. No new endpoint to configure, rotate or publish.

boundary: The write goes into the portal estate from the internal side. No internal list is touched in either direction, and the flow stays tenant-authenticated, so the crossing count stays at one.
verification: npm run wiring   # C7 appears with both operations and the boundary section stays clean
Patch a submission to review and read it back through STATUS - the citizen must see the new status and a second timeline event
Call ECM_DOCS_INTAKE with no action and confirm the feed is unchanged

standardConformance.decision: D7 - the standard work rides along with each visit rather than waiting for a sixth pass. The flow is already open, and adding a catch scope to a flow whose actions you have just rewritten costs a fraction of coming back to it.
standardConformance.order: Do the standard work FIRST, before the SharePoint actions in Step B. The variables and Scope_Global have to exist before an action can reference them, and moving actions into a scope afterwards is where things get dropped.

missing.title: Initialise the standard variable set
missing.how: Three Initialize variable actions at the very top of the flow, before Scope_Global.
missing.why: One response envelope can only serve every flow if every flow reports its outcome the same way.

missing.title: Initialise the timing variables
missing.how: Four more Initialize variable actions, alongside the core set.

alsoAdd.name: Scope_Finalize_Response_State
alsoAdd.where: Inside Scope_Global, after the work and before the envelope

missing.why: The envelope and the run record both report timing. Computing it once is what keeps them agreeing.

missing.title: Wrap the work in Scope_Global
missing.how: Add a Scope named Scope_Global and move every existing action except the Initialize variable actions inside it.
missing.why: One place to attach a catch. Without it the failure path has to be repeated on every branch, which is why the flows missing this are the same flows missing a catch.

missing.title: Answer through the standard envelope
missing.how: Add a Compose named Compose__Standard_Response_Revised as the last action inside Scope_Global, before the Response.
missing.why: core/contracts.js unwraps exactly this shape. A flow answering anything else has to be special-cased in the client, which is how one-off shapes accumulate.

missing.title: Redact headers before capture
missing.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Redacted_Headers, running after Compose_Redacted_Queries.
missing.why: Without it the observability harness becomes the leak.

wireInto.note: Same: an unconsumed Compose redacts nothing. Compose_Flow_Run_Record must also be moved to run after Compose_Redacted_Headers, or it composes before the value exists.

missing.title: Redact the query string before capture
missing.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Redacted_Queries. Place it first in that scope, immediately after Get_Flow_Definition.
missing.why: sig is the trigger credential and code is the one-time password. On the verification flows this is the difference between telemetry and a log of every OTP issued.

wireInto.note: Adding the Compose without this leaves it inert: the run record captures no query string at all, and the conformance check still passes. The rule is about what reaches telemetry, not about an action existing.
